findings: REPLACES AN AMOSTOOLS STUB. Until 2026-08-12 this row held only the token table with the library stripped out from under it -- both length fields zero, no code, every routine word overwritten with `====` -- so the tier could not rise above `manual`. The real library's table is IDENTICAL to the stub's, entry for entry, id for id and spec for spec, which is a check on the AMOSTools reader as much as on this registration. What changes is that the code is now here to read. IT SHIPS IN BOTH HOST BUILDS and both are held: `AMOSPRO_Int.Lib` (AMOS Pro, 24,688 bytes, the one registered) and `Int.Lib` (AMOS 1.3, 24,212 bytes, sha256 95f64c08440f7ec83041e365bf2c495dcb539fc674901224c6bde1358f32e7a7). Their jump-table and token-table lengths are IDENTICAL -- $ca and $5c0 -- so the whole 476-byte difference is in the code. That makes the pair a controlled comparison of what the two hosts need from the same extension, which nothing else in the registry offers. NOT THE SAME EXTENSION AS jd-int-1.3 despite both prefixing `wb `: five names in common and zero ids in common. THE ARCHIVE CARRIES TWO MORE EXTENSIONS, and one of them settles a standing gap. `Intuition_1.3_Demo/` holds Intuition.Lib in both flavours (AMOS 1.3, 41,284 bytes; AMOS Pro, 40,676) -- the intuition-1.3b row was until now the ONE registered port with no binary at all. Two cautions before that row moves off `manual`: this is 1.3 and not 1.3b, which bears directly on the five keyword names the two builds disagree about; and it is a DEMO that warns at run time "Intuition.lib: warning: Can't open reqtools.library v38.  Some commands may not work properly", so some routines may be stubbed. Its two builds differ in TOKEN TABLE size ($25e against $232), so unlike Int they are not one table twice. `Intuition_1.6/AMOSPro_IntuiExt_1.6.lib` is a third copy of IntuiExtend 1.6, with its own examples and data directory.
notes: Opens Workbench windows and screens from AMOS, with menus and mouse reading.
